title: Special Edition: The Shield Hero’s Valentine’s Day Part 12
text: “That’s right, this guy is the boss of the Chocolate Monsters!”
A Chocolate Monster writhing inside a test tube. This guy is the boss?
“A few hours ago, I caught him after he got snagged in one of my traps—the ones I set up in the mountains to catch thieves who steal my inventions!”

…Seriously? Not only did the boss of the Chocolate Monsters get caught in a trap, but the fact that he was conveniently captured is pretty outrageous too. Why on earth would a chocolate farmer even set traps in the mountains in the first place? Nobody’s going to want your inventions. At the very least, you should’ve made it a trap specifically for chocolate thieves.
“Oh, right. So? How are you going to use that Chocolate Monster as an ingredient for your finished Horse Manure Chocolate?”
“Hmph. That’s why you’re so stupid. You can’t even figure out the result just by looking at this?”

I’m not some kind of psychic. …There are several possibilities. I don’t know the details of this monster’s ecology, but I’m not ruling out the idea of harvesting from the chocolate monster. But… knowing this jerk of an old man, he’s probably thinking along even worse lines. The kind of thing that’ll make me feel even worse.
“Yeah, yeah. So?”

I’ll take a step back, get the details out of him, and then figure out how to handle this. Just in case it turns out to be a brilliant invention, I’ll hold off on rejecting it outright. After all, there’s a history of heroes who shot down ideas right from the start and ended up getting their asses kicked. I’ll at least listen to what he has to say. After that, I’ll just take my time cleaning up the mess.

“Well then, listen up. I’m going to combine this Chocolate Monster with a Horse (the name of a horse-shaped monster) and a Filolial, and改造 it into a monster that produces horse-manure chocolate no matter what it eats! Perfect! I’ll use your Filolial for the experiment!”
“No way!”

Chick spoke!? She seemed to really hate the idea, so she stopped acting and ran away. Does she hate it that much…? Of course she does! I’d hate it too if I were in her shoes. I’d rather die than end up like that.

But, as expected—or rather, it was a truly awful invention. Combining a Chocolate Monster with a monster to make horse-dung chocolate… that’s not chocolate—it’s shit. Does he really plan to make that prototype using real, living monsters?! There might be people who think, “As long as I don’t see the production process, it’s fine to eat!” but this will turn that niche product into something absolutely inedible.
This asshole of an old man—his inventions have completely gone off the rails. It’s a classic case of things getting worse the more he tries to create something new.
“If you’re going to run, then call the Sword Hero… Ren and Taniko!”

I shout at Chick as she runs away. The Chocolate Monster, which is going to be the victim of such a crazy and ridiculous invention, is the one I really feel sorry for. It would surely have a better life if it were protected by Taniko and the others. In more ways than one, I want to deal with this before anyone gets hurt.
“Don’t run awayyyyyy!”
The jerk of a dad, who was yelling and stomping after Chick, hurried back into the workshop the moment I took a single step forward.
“What are you planning to do?”
“It’s obvious—I’m going to take care of this crazy, self-proclaimed inventor who doesn’t give a damn about bothering others.”
“Don’t you dare interfere with my inventions! Die!”
The jerk of a old man starts flinging trash from inside the workshop at me. But I’m the Shield Hero. Throwing attacks from an ordinary person don’t even scratch me.
“I’ll eliminate any intruders!”
The moment I set foot inside the workshop, a hole opens up in the platform I was standing on. What kind of trap is this? The money used to build this facility—it’s not my money, is it?
Well, traps like this don’t work on me. Using the flight ability from my barbarian armor, I maintain my altitude and take a step forward.
“Ugh! You monster! Take this!”
Next, a spiked wall shoots out at me from the side with great force. I reach out my hand toward the wall and stop it with a thud. Something like this won’t even leave a scratch.
“Give it up already. Your pathetic inventions end today.”
“Not yet! Don’t underestimate my traps for exterminating intruders!”

With a clang, heated chocolate rained down on me from the duct above. Under normal circumstances, this would be more than just a burn. Plus, once it hardens, it’s no joke. Well, as the Shield Hero, something like this won’t even make me wince.
“Shooting Star Shield”
Just to be safe, I quietly cast the skill.
“‘Shield Hero!’”
The Robin Hood’s mother and sister cried out.
“Huh, hahahahahaha!”
That bastard of a father was cackling. Does he seriously think he’s taken me down? Does he really believe he can kill the hero who saved the world with a trap like this?
“Haha—What?!”
The chocolate, heated by the Shooting Star Shield, is deflected and trickles down. Then I stood calmly before that bastard of a father.
“Are you an idiot? Setting up a trap like this… No one’s ever going to come steal your pathetic inventions.”
“You’re the thief who stole my inventions!”
“A thief? Nope. I’m the messenger here to deliver bitter reality and punishment to a crazy, would-be inventor. The ‘Hero’ thing? That’s all in the past!”

After coldly retorting to that jerk of a dad, who was pointing at me and yelling, I turned my gaze to Raphtalia, who was holding a hammer. The weapon was… that beep-beep hammer I’d made her copy the other day. It’s not lethal, but I hear it has a status effect that causes unconsciousness. There’s absolutely no room to go easy on him. This guy really never does anything right.
“Please stay still for a moment.”
Raphtalia leaped to my side in an instant and brought the Beep-Beep Hammer down on the jerk’s head.
“Nuuuuuuuuuuh! I’m—guh!?”

The jerk tried to resist, but Raphtalia’s Beep-Beep Hammer hit him in the head, and he passed out. I roughly picked up the old man, who had fallen onto his back, and tossed him at the feet of the Robin Hood’s mother and sister.
“Raphtalia, it’ll be a hassle if he starts causing trouble when he comes to. Tie him up.”
“Yes… It’s been a while since I’ve met someone so… unusual.”
“Unusual,” huh. That’s putting it pretty mildly.
“Exactly. It’s truly ridiculous. At this rate, the Trash from the past might actually have been better.”
“I wonder how he’d fare if compared to the Trash from back then…”
True. It’s actually more puzzling how a Trash like this can even exist in a world that’s overcome the waves. I look at the captured Chocolate Monster. Hmm… something feels off about it.

It has a star on its forehead… it looks like sludge, and it’s bigger than the one I encountered before. If you call it a boss, I suppose it is, but it also looks pretty much the same as a regular Chocolate Monster. Well, since Fitoria, the boss of the Filolials, usually takes the form of an ordinary Filolial, maybe you can’t tell just by looking at it.
“What’s going on? The Filolial pulling Naofumi’s carriage asked us to come right away—what happened?”

Just then, Ren and the others rushed over. They looked confused, unable to make sense of the situation. That makes sense. If I were in their shoes, I wouldn’t think there’d be a Chocolate Monster boss in a place like this either.
“Ah, I took care of one crazy idiot. There was a monster captured there, and I was thinking of having Ren and Taniko take a look at it.”
“For once, just call her by her name, Wyndia.”
“…This one?”

Taniko let out a sigh as if she’d given up and looked at the captured chocolate monster I was pointing at. She was fascinated. I couldn’t tell if it was really the boss. Knowing this jerk of a dad, there’s a good chance he’s just making stuff up.
“Ah.”
“I think this is probably the boss we were looking for… It seems different from the others.”
“Ren, what about you?”
“His appearance doesn’t match what I remember from the game… but there’s a lingering trace of him in the stars.”
Just as I thought… it seems this is indeed the boss Ren and the others were looking for. I figured there must be a reason, so I called him over—and I was right.
“What should we do? Should we take him out?”
“The Valentine’s Day monsters are running wild, right? Will things calm down if we defeat this guy?”
“I guess so…”
Taniko approaches the captured Chocolate Monster boss and speaks to it.
“Yeah… yeah. I get it.”
Then she comes over to us.
“Did you manage to communicate with it?”
“Yeah. It seems this one was the main body.”
“So? What were you two talking about?”
“It seemed angry because the folks around here were neglecting chocolate. I wonder if there used to be a festival held here regularly?”
“Isn’t this guy actually the cause? It didn’t seem like he was running away—more like he was looking for someone to take his anger out on.”
Stomping on that jerk of a dad, I ask Taniko.
“That seems to be part of it, too. That’s why they gave us a grace period…”
A festival, huh… What exactly do they do there?
“Anyway, even if we defeat this guy, he won’t die, right?”
“It’s not that it can’t die, but it’s rooted in this land, and it seems to revive when the time comes.”
Is it the type that parasitizes the land or something? Maybe it’s the boss of this Chocolate Zone?
“Besides, this one isn’t the only main body…”
“Is that so?”
“Yeah, we’ve taken down a few so far. Defeating them does calm things down in the area for a while, but it’s not a fundamental solution, right?”
“True. It’d be a pain if they kept popping up every year.”

I don’t know about asking adventurers to hunt them down or whatever, but it’s better to wipe out these kinds of nuisances at the root. Apparently, the root cause is a festival… it seems like they neglected to perform some ritual involving these things. Even though it was originally something a hero spread, now the chocolate itself has taken on a mind of its own and is running amok… Is there some kind of divine will at work here?
Killing gods is my job—and Raphtalia’s, though. A “Aragami,” is that what they’re called? Like a yokai? Are they in the same category?
“For now, let’s keep them under protection, and if there are any problems, we’ll just have to put them down, right?”
“Yeah. That’s fine. I’ll handle asking about the festival, so please protect the areas where the monsters are spawning.”
“If that’s what it takes to calm things down, isn’t that good enough?”
“Yeah. That’s why she’s coming along with us.”
“So we’re bringing them to the village…”

What a hassle… Well, if the research on the chocolate monsters goes well, it’ll probably make some money, so I guess it’s fine. But what’s the deal with that creature living at my place? I mean, it might be okay this time of year, but that depends on how long it lasts. It’ll be a problem if it stays all year round. I’ll leave those details to Taniko and Rat.
“Now, what should I do about this jerk of an old man?”
“What did you do to make Lord Iwatani so angry?”
“First, he flaunted that vulgar invention called ‘Horse Manure Chocolate,’ and apparently, he wanted to create this Chocolate Monster’s boss by genetically engineering a horse and a Filolial.”
“Who on earth would eat such a tasteless food?”

The female knight’s point is valid. In my world, I suppose there’d be people who’d eat it as long as they didn’t know the actual manufacturing process. I mean, just look at the food coloring and ingredients—there’s a lot of sketchy stuff in there. Even so, I’d hate to think of a Filolial or a horse being used to produce chocolate.
“According to this guy’s logic, it was supposed to be something everyone would want. Do you really think it would sell?”
“…I’m sorry, Lord Iwatani, but I don’t think so.”
“Did I say it would sell?”
“No…”

There are limits to what you can joke about, right? Besides, if people saw how it’s made, nobody would eat it. …Come to think of it, I seem to recall hearing a story about making tea out of Elephant dung. That thought crosses my mind, but I’ll just ignore it.

Taniko looks annoyed and glares at that jerk of a father. After all, a monster was almost turned into a toy. Of course she’d be angry. For what it’s worth, the “Robin Hood”’s mother and sister are watching with concern. It seems there’s still some family affection there. But we should turn him in where he belongs.
“For now, since this guy has done something that could make him a criminal, we’ll turn him in where he belongs.”
“Y-yes.”

“I think I’ll temporarily delegate management authority to you guys under the Hero’s authority… though I’ll have to ask the guy who runs the chocolate farms around here for the details. If you’re short on manpower, just say so—the guys working for me will come help out.”
“I’ll give you a discount for that, though.” With that added, we handed the jerk of a dad over to the vigilante group and threw him in the holding cell.

I don’t expect it, but if he’s truly repentant, he’ll behave himself. If he acts up, the authority over the chocolate farm will be transferred to the Robin Hood’s mother and sister, and this guy will lose all his rights. I don’t know what happens after that. It’s a fitting end for Trash who doesn’t give a damn about the people around him.
And so, we bought chocolate from the farm run by the Robin Hood’s parents and transported the Chocolate Monster boss to the village.
And then…
“Oh? What’s the matter, Lord Iwatani?”
I went through a portal to meet the Trash—the Wise King of Wisdom and the Hero of the Staff—who was attending to official business at the castle.
“Trash, bow your head to me.”
“If that is what Lord Iwatani desires, I shall do so. If it means Lord Iwatani can get along with Melty.”
“Haahhh…”
I let out a huge, deep sigh without even realizing it.
“Never mind.”

If I’d made him bow right then, Trash would’ve probably started promising all sorts of things—true or false—as if they were facts. Even in that exchange just now, if I’d made him bow, he’d likely have pushed for a marriage with Melty or something. Man… Trash’s on a whole different level from that shitty old man. You really don’t go down without a fight.
Trash tilted his head. I guess he really can’t figure it out.
“Something must have happened. I’ll do my best to appease Lord Iwatani’s anger.”
Even so, he’s found some reason to understand.
“No, it’s fine. Just get back to work.”
“H-huh…”
“By the way, Trash.”
“What is it?”
“Aren’t you working on any inventions or anything?”
“I’m researching ways to cut costs on the Magical Power crystals and sound crystals used for lighting at the venue Melty is organizing. Here are the documents.”

I’m shown pages crammed with theories on making Magical Power crystals usable by anyone, along with the logic for deriving the optimal parameters to maintain their luminescence. Wow… they’re pouring this much technology into such a trivial thing? It’s like LED technology.
“I was just thinking I’d like you to try out the prototype, Lord Iwatani.”

I take the prototype from Trash. Am I supposed to infuse this with Magical Power? I gently channel some Magical Power into it. The crystal glows incredibly brightly, blinding me. Huh? It’s bright, but it doesn’t hurt my eyes.

Wow… they’ve really put a lot of thought into this. With this, it’ll function as lighting for a long time even with just a tiny amount of Magical Power. It’s worlds apart from that idiot who made that horse-dung chocolate. Even though he calls himself “I”… the Wise King of Wisdom is still going strong, even in these peaceful times.
“Yeah. With this, the next event should go smoothly.”
“As you command, Lord Iwatani…”
Well, that’s how my days go by.
